thread.title_full: Whitmer pushes back against potential gas tax holiday as prices grow above $4 - NewsBreak

author: David Sackrider
title: Whitmer pushes back against potential gas tax holiday as prices grow above $4 - NewsBreak
text:
By David Sackrider ,
5 hours ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — Gas prices continue to rise across Mid-Michigan as the war with Iran continues. In Lansing, the average price sits right around $4.15 per gallon, according to AAA. The price is up 20 cents from last week, and over a dollar more than this time a month ago.
State lawmakers have options when it comes to attempting to reduce financial pressure on Michiganders. One potential avenue would be to suspend Michigan’s gas tax, by declaring a state tax holiday for a period of time.
(WLNS) Speaking with reporters in Grand Rapids on March 18, Governor Gretchen Whitmer is pushing back on the proposal.
“One state can’t address all the pressures that we’re feeling because of this war in Iran, but we will continue to do what we can to put money in people’s pockets,” she said. “That’s what we’ve done with you know, as people are filing their taxes right now, many people are getting historic refunds thanks to the earned income tax credit.”
The governor did not fully rule out the measure, saying that she did not want to “over promise” something that would be hard to deliver.
(WLNS) Michigan would not be the first to pass such a tax break. On Friday, Georgia Governor Brian Kemp signed a 60-day tax holiday, and lawmakers in Connecticut and Tennessee have floated similar proposals.
The measure is also something state lawmakers have considered in the past. Back in 2022, when prices reached $4.32 per gallon, a 6-month gas tax holiday did pass the state legislature, but it was vetoed by the governor.
At that time, the gas tax included a six percent sales tax in addition to a 31-cent motor fuel tax. Whitmer had shown interest in pausing the sales tax, but not the motor fuel tax.
In 2026, however, state lawmakers altered the gas tax to remove the sales tax and increase the motor fuel tax to 52.4 cents per gallon.
There are potential consequences to providing the tax break. In just 60 days, Georgia’s gas tax holiday is estimated to cost the state between $360 million and $400 million. Their tax is also 19 cents less than Michigan’s, which could create a larger impact in the Great Lake State.
Almost all of the money generated by the tax is used to fund road projects throughout the state.
(WLNS) While Michigan could see a huge hit to the budget by pausing the tax, the potential savings for the average Michigander is much smaller. At $4.15 per gallon, a 15-gallon tank of gas costs just over $62.25. Removing the gas tax takes the price down to $3.63 per gallon, or $54.39 for the same amount of gas, a savings of just $7.86.
“Between tariffs and this increase in gas prices, we know that people are feeling the pinch, and we’ll continue to try to work to give people relief where we can,” Whitmer said.
A gas tax holiday would require sign off from Republicans in the House of Representatives and Democrats in the Senate. 6 News reached out to see where Speaker of the House Matt Hall stands on the proposal, but did not hear back at this time
